text:
anika: Proposal: split session-tiling out of inference-runtime into a tiny hotpath tiler service + a separate metadata-plane service for profiles/rollouts. Objective: faster runtime deploys, clearer kv ownership, and smaller blast radius for model-profile changes.

matt: High level +1. Two immediate concerns: 1) RPC cost on hotpath, 2) ensuring no visible staleness for in-flight sessions.

anika: Agreed. Design choices:
- tiler: co-located, process-local or sidecar to preserve sub-200us p95. Responsible for batching, prefix-tiling logic, and KV cache of active sessions.
- metadata-plane: centralized, eventual-consistent store for model_profile, quant_profile, rollout_state, plus audit/logs. Exposes read API and async notify stream for tiler caches.

ricardo: How do we migrate existing keys? We still have runtime-owned kv prefixes in production.

anika: Migration outline:
1) Introduce versioned prefixes: e.g., sessions:v2:tiler and modelmeta:v2. Runtime will read v1 and write v1+v2 during dual-write window.
2) Shadow reads: tiler will perform parallel reads from v2 on a subset (10%) of traffic and log diffs to reconciliation queue.
3) Reconciliation worker will heal mismatches and emit metrics.
4) Flip reads to v2 in waves by tenant.

lila: Reconciliation worker is key. Does it need writeback permission? What about conflict resolution?

ricardo: Suggest deterministic tie-breaker: use write-timestamp and canonical owner = metadata-plane for profile objects. Tiler resolves conflicts by accepting metadata-plane state unless a transient write is in progress. Reconciler writes repaired v2 keys and emits audit events.

matt: What metrics should we watch during rollout?

anika: Minimum set:
- tiler.batch_efficiency (tokens/request vs baseline)
- tiler.rpc_p95_delta (vs baseline runtime p95)
- metadata.staleness_ms (observed diff between write and tiler cache refresh)
- reconciliation.queue_depth and mismatch_rate
- session.failover_count when fallback path used

ops-bot: [canary] deploying inference-tiler:v0.1-canary to dev - 2/2 pods ready, p95 +85us.

lila: Rollback plan? If tiler causes tail latency spikes we need immediate fallback.

anika: Runtime will keep an opt-in local tiler shim (small copy of tiling logic) behind a feature flag. Default behavior: call tiler; if RPC fails or p95 > threshold, fail open to local shim. Also an emergency admin toggle to force local-only tiling per tenant.

matt: Sounds good. Also ensure the tiler exposes a lightweight diagnostic endpoint (/debug/last-ops) and health checks for canary autoscaler to use.

ricardo: Schema ownership: metadata-plane is canonical for model_profile, quant_profile, rollout_state. Runtime/tiler caches are read-only caches with TTL and subscription invalidation via Kafka-style topic for updates.

anika: Subscription details: metadata-plane publishes small delta events on profile changes. Tiler subscribes and invalidates keys. For safety, tiler also does periodic full-syncs (configurable; default 60s).

lila: How long will dual-write run? We need an exit criteria.

anika: Dual-write window: until mismatch_rate < 0.01% and reconciliation queue depth = 0 for 48h for target tenants. We’ll automate checks and require sign-off from owners.

matt: Security/ACLs? metadata-plane will be accessed by admin-plane + tiler. Use tenant-scoped tokens and mTLS; tighten admin APIs behind ACL.

devx-bot: Reminder: RFC template checklist missing compatibility contract link.

anika: Action items:
- anika -> fork RFC and write canonical contract (fields, canonical owner, read semantics).
- matt -> prototype tiler sidecar and measure p95 at load.
- ricardo -> build reconciliation worker and diff metrics.
- lila -> define rollout waves and runbook; author emergency toggles.
- ev: (ops) add canary abort rules: abort if tiler.rpc_p95_delta > 2x or error_rate > 0.5% for 3m.

ops-bot: [canary] inference-tiler:v0.1-canary - observed p95 +120us on staging synthetic load.

anika: Oof. If staging p95 is +120us we should iterate on co-location and batching behavior. Matt, please try process-shared placement next.

matt: Will do. Also will experiment with a tiny in-memory hot cache in tiler to avoid some RPCs for repeated prefixes.

ricardo: Reconciler design note: keep write-idempotency and process-at-least-once semantics. We'll expose a /replay endpoint for manual audits.

lila: Runbook pre-checks before tenant flip: reconciliation zeroed, recent full-sync completed, no open rollouts, health ok for tiler pods for 30m. Add a metric dashboard panel for quick go/no-go.

anika: Example admin commands (for demos):

curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://admin.internal/flags -d '{"tenant":"acme","flag":"tiler_dual_write","state":"on"}'

curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://admin.internal/flags -d '{"tenant":"acme","flag":"tiler_reads","state":"on"}'

matt: Timeline: two-week spike to prototype sidecar, week 3 run staging canary with synthetic traffic, week 5 start tenant waves if numbers look good.

anika: Good. Keep incremental and observable. We want to reduce runtime deploy times by decoupling churn, but not at the cost of tail latency.

lila: I'll schedule a tabletop incident drill for the rollback scenario.

anika: Thanks all. We'll iterate on placement and cache heuristics. Please add any additional failure modes to the RFC PR comments. :thumbsup:
